changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: A name, not a queue. For your biggest on-sales you get a named person and a stated on-call commitment: someone who picks up. For buyers who run high-volume events, especially operations executives. Publish the commitment only once the team can staff it, and drop 'tiers' and 'response times' as headline terms.
changes.why: The COO answered our tiers pitch with 'a queue with a faster timer' and described the need as 'a name, not a queue' and 'someone who picks up', never using the word 'support'.

changes.change: New line and one-page asset for high-volume event buyers: 'On-sale morning, minute four: who's watching, who you call, and what happens next. Here is the plan, on paper, with the names on it.' Build the on-sale readiness plan template with the solutions engineer and use it in evaluations with operations executives.
changes.why: The COO asked to see on paper what we do on an on-sale morning ('who's watching, who she calls, what happens at minute four'), and we had no such artifact.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For high-volume event and ticketing buyers, replace the logo-led 'see our customer stories' with a reference from a ticketing or on-sale customer who can say in their own words who picked up when it mattered. Lead with that person's account, not the logo wall.
changes.why: The rep said 'I had logos. I didn't have a person,' and the decider wanted a person's account of an on-sale rather than generic proof.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Do not lead with the developer and technical story (APIs, sandbox, load tests) for operations-executive deciders. Keep it for the technical evaluator, and open with the customer's framing for the executive: 'I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.'
changes.why: The sandbox load test went great with the CTO but drew a one-word 'good.' from the COO, who made the call alone and said she buys behaviour during failure, not uptime.
